evidence_grade: A: local regression tests and implementation inspection

verification.baseline: Before the fixes, the initial 21 regression methods reported 24 assertion failures and one configuration error; every finding had a failing case. The configuration error was the new exact-code exemption, whose underlying false positive also had a separate assertion failure.
verification.focused: 22 regression methods passed after fixes, including an additional custom-assertion waiver check.
verification.full_suite: Final full suite: 152 tests passed in 384.629 seconds (exit 0).
verification.lint: Ruff 0.17.1 from an existing offline cache: all checks passed.
verification.syntax: compileall passed for src, tests, and examples.
verification.demo: The real CLI demo passed: hollow proof rejected, valid proof red=1/green=0, readiness passed, delivery remained blocked without human approval.
verification.network: No network services used. The partial-clone regression uses a local file upstream and a sentinel transport that cannot contact a remote. No push or publishing commands were executed.

findings.change: Preflight rejects every restored path absent from HEAD but already present locally, including ignored files, dangling symlinks, and directories, before any source restoration.
findings.evidence: All three path kinds retain their original local contents or link target; the source fix stays intact.

findings.change: PreToolUse installs onFailure=block and an explicit timeout covering all configured checks plus a margin. A shorter POSIX adapter deadline permits cleanup and deny JSON. Catchable interrupts and SystemExit are denied. Supported minimum Claude Code version is 2.1.310.
findings.evidence: Installed policy and timeout are asserted; a real check sends SIGTERM to the adapter, which emits parseable deny JSON and exits zero. Installed Claude Code 2.1.310 command-hook schema and failure-handling code were inspected locally for onFailure support; no model session or push was invoked.

findings.change: Attempt start atomically invalidates old proof with state=running and ok=false. Only a completed attempt publishes state=complete. Gate rejects incomplete attempts and residual restoration plans, including with a waiver.
findings.evidence: After a valid empty-output proof, a second green phase sends a real SIGINT. CLI exits 130; old success cannot be reused and the next gate fails.

findings.change: Red and green use distinct fresh Python bytecode-cache prefixes and disable cache writes; existing user caches are untouched.
findings.evidence: A real imported function changes from 21 to 42 with equal source length and a forced identical timestamp. An existing stale pyc remains byte-for-byte unchanged; red exits 1 and green exits 0.

findings.change: Snapshot all reverted paths by contents, type, and full mode. Save differences in redgreen-mutations.json, alongside the Git patch, before restoration; reserve that sidecar against attachment overlap.
findings.evidence: Writes, chmod, and replacement with a symlink on a baseline-only deleted file each fail the proof, skip green, and retain before/after evidence. Content bytes are recoverable from the saved JSON.

findings.change: Find JavaScript callback bodies after argument objects or destructured parameters rather than balancing the first brace in the call.
findings.evidence: Options objects, destructured arrow callbacks, and function callbacks retain assertions; an assertion-free destructured callback still fails.

findings.change: Separate code and comment views. Debug checks ignore strings/comments; unfinished markers apply only to comments. Add visible exact-line allowed_code_lines exemptions for those checks.
findings.evidence: Business strings and regexes containing debugger, TODO, or console.log pass. A multiline TODO comment fails. Exact exemptions are warned visibly and whitespace changes stop matching.

findings.change: Focused-test scanning recognizes only followed by a call chain, including parameterized each and tagged tables.
findings.evidence: Both test.only.each and describe.only.each fail in call and template-table forms.

findings.change: Inspect Python assertion argument ASTs: comparisons and behavior calls count as behavioral, while simple truthiness and existence checks remain weak.
findings.evidence: assertTrue/assertFalse comparisons and predicates pass; bare values, exists(), and constant true remain flagged.

findings.change: Recognize Go Testify assertions, import aliases, formatted variants, and receivers created with New. Custom assertion frameworks can use a visible weak_test_justification without waiving red/green.
findings.evidence: require.Equal/NoError, aliased imports, and New receivers pass; assertion-free tests fail. A reasoned custom-framework waiver yields a warning and still requires V2.

findings.change: Use language-specific test-entry matchers; Rust test attributes no longer collide with JavaScript test(...) matching.
findings.evidence: A Rust function named test with assert_eq! passes as one block; its assertion-free counterpart fails.

findings.change: Recognize should_panic attributes associated with Rust test functions as behavior assertions.
findings.evidence: Both should_panic and should_panic(expected=...) forms pass without a redundant assert macro.

findings.change: Apply junk-path failures only to files still present at HEAD; retain deletion statistics.
findings.evidence: Deleting a committed build output and synthetic key file passes hygiene while preserving removed-line and file entries.

findings.change: Recognize JavaScript regex literals and escapes before scanning for comment delimiters.
findings.evidence: A URL-scheme regex produces no comment finding; a real trailing comment is still extracted.

findings.change: Pass only extracted comment text to authorship inspection while matching exemptions against the original complete source line.
findings.evidence: A synthetic authorship string beside a harmless comment passes. The same phrase in an actual comment fails unless its exact source line is exempted.

findings.change: Installer and dry-run JSON contain only owned hook entries, destination path, version requirement, and status; unrelated settings remain only on disk.
findings.evidence: A synthetic service token remains in the saved env object and never appears on stdout in preview or actual installation. Existing settings and idempotence remain covered.

findings.change: All internal Git operations force no lazy fetching and disable every transport protocol. Partial clones require Git's no-lazy-fetch capability; absent objects fail with a local preparation instruction.
findings.evidence: In a real blob:none clone, a missing old blob remains absent after Repo.blob and the hygiene CLI. A sentinel promisor transport is never invoked, despite a permissive local transport setting and a caller-set lazy-fetch restriction.

findings.change: Same root cause and cache-isolation fix as C4; this does more than disabling bytecode writes.
findings.evidence: The real unittest import distinguishes the equal-length 21-to-42 fix despite a deliberately stale existing cache and identical source timestamps.

findings.change: Choose the documented limitation rather than adding a Rust rewriter. Error text and both READMEs explicitly say that every changed Rust production file containing inline tests is rejected, even with unchanged inline tests and a separate new regression.
findings.evidence: The unchanged-inline-test reproduction returns the precise limitation. Separating only the new test is no longer suggested as sufficient.

limitations: No hosted Claude Code model session was started; hook protocol, generated policy, real adapter signals, and installed host implementation were checked locally.
Python commands overriding the cache environment and non-Python build caches require an appropriate clean-build recipe.
Lexical hygiene remains heuristic; documented exceptions are visible and do not replace behavioral proof.
Mixed Rust production/inline-test red-green rewriting remains unsupported and is now documented accurately.
No human approval, commit, push, or publication was performed.
